events.description: Panda-themed street festival on Pennsylvania Avenue with Asian street food (mochi, garlic noodles), face painting, live performances, bounce houses, and cultural celebrations. A traveling family-friendly gathering spotlighting panda and Asian culture.

events.title: District Vibes / American Pride Exhibition Tour (Accessible Edition)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library – Central Library
events.description: Guided tours of the District Vibes / American Pride exhibit, commemorating DC's 250th-anniversary contributions to American culture through images, artifacts, and history. The August 22 Saturday tour includes visually descriptive language for blind or low-vision visitors. Registration encouraged.

events.title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, DC
events.time: Sat: Practice/IROC from ~10 AM; Sun: Race 1:00 PM ET
events.venue: National Mall Street Circuit (Pennsylvania Ave, Constitution Ave, Independence Ave)
events.price: Free general admission (GA lottery now closed; paid VIP available)
events.description: The first-ever NTT INDYCAR SERIES race on the National Mall — a historic 1.7-mile, 7-turn street circuit past the Washington Monument, U.S. Capitol, and National Archives. Saturday features IROC Exhibition with NASCAR/IndyCar legends (Gordon, Castroneves, Franchitti, etc.) and free autograph sessions. Sunday's main race airs live on FOX at 1 PM. A signature America 250 celebration with Smithsonian kids' zones and racing simulators. Note: GA lottery is closed; street access is broadly free.

events.title: Improvapalooza 2026 – Washington Improv Theater
events.venue: Washington Improv Theater at Studio Theatre
events.price: Nightly passes $25 (+$2.47 service fee); All-Palooza Pass $80
events.description: WIT's community-beloved marathon of experimental improv comedy — more than 200 shows over five days. Expect outlandish costumes, big ideas, and big laughs. Each show is completely different. Festival-style, first-come seating. Runs Wed Aug 19 through Mon Aug 24, overlapping the Aug 22–23 weekend.

events.title: Eastern Market Main Street – Free Friday Jazz Under the Shed (August Fridays)
events.venue: Eastern Market Farmer's Line Shed, 225 7th St SE
events.description: Every Friday evening in August, relax under the shade of the Eastern Market farmer's line shed for free live jazz. Sponsored by Jason Secrest / Coldwell Banker. August 7 featured Amy K. Bormet; subsequent Fridays (Aug 14, 21, 28) continue the series.

events.title: DCPL Back-to-School Family Events (System-Wide)
events.description: Throughout August, DC Public Library branches across the city host free back-to-school events featuring bookbag and school supply giveaways, games, crafts, face painting, live entertainment, and wellness resources. Families can also sign up for free library cards.

events.title: Events DC Community Cooldown Summer Series – Ward Activations
events.time: 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM (based on confirmed Aug 4 instance)
events.venue: The Fields Pavilion @ RFK Campus / Various Ward locations
events.description: Events DC's Community Cooldown Summer Series brings free sweets, music, and family-friendly activities to all 8 Wards. Past activations at The Fields Pavilion @ RFK have featured JumpDC Superstars and DJs. Check eventsdc.com for August 15–29 ward-specific dates.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at the Kennedy Center REACH
events.description: Outdoor film screenings running through August 29 on the Kennedy Center's REACH Campus. A free, family-friendly way to enjoy movies under the summer sky.

events.title: The Fields at RFK Campus – Open Play / Community Recreational Fields

events.description: The Fields at RFK Campus is a 27-acre outdoor sports complex on the Anacostia River with turf fields, bike paths, and a celebration pavilion. Open to the community for recreational play; check eventsdc.com for any programmed weekend activations during these dates.

events.title: The Notebook
events.price: From ~$57 (resale avg ~$210); TodayTix rush/lottery may apply
events.description: The Broadway touring production of The Notebook, based on the best-selling novel and iconic film. Plays the weekends of Aug 22–23 and Aug 29–30.

events.title: USBG America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration (Ongoing Exhibit)
events.description: A garden-wide exhibit showcasing the flowers chosen by all U.S. states and territories to represent them, celebrating America's 250th anniversary. Also on view: 'Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise,' exploring unique plant survival adaptations. Admission is always free; no tickets required.

events.title: DC Summer Restaurant Week
events.description: DC's biannual celebration of its dining scene — hundreds of restaurants citywide offer special fixed-price menus at $25, $35, and $55 price points all month long.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Outdoor Market – Saturday
events.description: Eastern Market's Saturday Market runs through September 26, 2026, featuring farmers, artists, crafters, and prepared food sellers along 7th St SE from Pennsylvania Ave to North Carolina Ave. Streets, sidewalks, and adjoining plazas fill with vendors.

events.title: District Vibes / American Pride: How DC Changed American Culture (Exhibit)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library, 901 G St NW
events.description: Free exhibit exploring DC's vibrant cultural contributions — from the football huddle to the modern blood bank to legends like Marvin Gaye — through images, artifacts, and storytelling. Satellite locations across the city; main site at MLK Library.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Outdoor Market – Sunday (Flea Market)
events.description: Eastern Market's Sunday Flea Market and outdoor market runs through September 27, 2026. Diverse vendors sell antiques, collectibles, handmade crafts, farm-fresh produce, and prepared food. One of DC's oldest and liveliest community marketplaces.

events.title: Venus
events.price: Single tickets TBA; Woolly Mammoth offers pay-what-you-can (PWYC) and $20-under-30 pricing
events.description: A world-premiere rolling world premiere by Steve Yockey, directed by new Artistic Director Reggie D. White. Follows orderly Nicole and instinctive Beth — two complete opposites whose love spirals into a darkly comedic tale of fear and obsession. Plays the weekends of Sep 12–13 and Sep 19–20.

events.title: America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration (Exhibit)
events.venue: U.S. Botanic Garden, 100 Maryland Ave SW
events.description: Celebrating America's 250th anniversary, the U.S. Botanic Garden showcases the official flowers of every U.S. state and territory — magnolias, roses, orchids, bluebonnets, saguaro cactus flowers, and more.
